title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk

epigraph.quote: In development real estate, pre-sales tell you what customers want today, collections tell you if they are paying for it, and launch-slippage tells you how honest management's calendar really is.
epigraph.author: Operational Underwriting Checklist

web_blocks.html: Because Ind AS 115 delays P&L revenue by 4–5 quarters, evaluating Ajmera requires tracking leading operational KPIs [10][11]. Watch pre-sales value (₹ Cr), carpet area sold (lakh sq ft), average realization (₹/sq ft), collections (₹ Cr), and net debt [10][11]. Between FY22 and FY26, annual pre-sales compounded nearly 4x [10][13][22]. Bookings rose from ₹431 crore in FY22 to ₹842 crore in FY23 (+95% YoY), ~₹1,017 crore in FY24, ₹1,084 crore in FY25, and ₹1,701 crore in FY26 (+57% YoY) [10][13][22]. Annual collections nearly tripled from ₹394 crore (FY22) and ₹532 crore (FY23) to ~₹645 crore (FY25) and ₹1,103 crore in FY26 (+71% YoY) [10][13]. That lifted collection efficiency from 60% in FY25 to 65% in FY26 [10]. Average realization also doubled from ₹12,083/sq ft in FY21 to ₹25,770/sq ft in FY26 as central Mumbai mix rose [10].

web_blocks.takeaway: Ajmera delivered a landmark FY26 beat (₹1,701 Cr pre-sales, ₹1,103 Cr collections), but H1 FY27 pre-sales of ₹307 Cr leave 86% of the ₹2,200 Cr FY27 target heavily back-ended into Q3–Q4 FY27 launches.

web_blocks.html: Management's forward pipeline is substantial as of Q2 FY27 (September 30, 2026) [14]. Ongoing and OC-received projects hold ₹3,510 crore of revenue visibility: ₹1,550 crore in committed sales pending recognition plus ₹1,960 crore in unsold inventory [14]. An upcoming 8-project launch pipeline adds ~₹7,008 crore across ~38 lakh sq ft [14]. Those launches span Wadala Boutique Office, Sion, Borivali, Whitefield, Doddaballapur, Yelahanka, and Vishrantwadi Pune [14]. Together, near-to-medium-term visibility exceeds ₹10,500+ crore [14]. Including the remaining Wadala land bank (~₹13,194 crore GDV), management pegs total long-term GDV potential at ~₹19,518 crore [10][14]. Estimated pre-tax post-debt cash flow across those project lifecycles stands at ₹3,900+ crore [10][14].

web_blocks.takeaway: Management has proven highly credible on balance-sheet deleveraging and Wadala/Vikhroli sales execution, but chronically over-optimistic on regulatory approval timelines—especially Kanjurmarg.

web_blocks.html: In Management's Own Words (Q2 FY27 Results & Call Commentary): On November 3, 2026, Director of Corporate Affairs Dhaval Ajmera highlighted balance-sheet discipline: "Backed by strong collections and asset monetisation, the Company reduced its debt by INR 34 crore to INR 646 crore as on 30th September 2026, while lowering its cost of debt to 10.75% p.a. from 11.01% p.a. in the previous quarter." [14] On H2 FY27 launch visibility, he added: "Looking ahead, the Company is actively pursuing the requisite approvals for its projects launch pipeline." [14] He expressed confidence that upcoming launches position Ajmera for a stronger second half, even as Kanjurmarg conversion stays gated by court and government clearances [14].

web_blocks.title: The H2 FY27 Bunching & Kanjurmarg Conversion Risk
paragraphs: Two execution flags stand out from the November 2026 (Q2 FY27) earnings call [14]. First, H1 FY27 pre-sales printed just ₹307 crore [14]. Hitting the ₹2,200 crore FY27 target requires ~₹1,893 crore of bookings in H2, heavily dependent on Q4 launches [14]. Those Q4 launches include Wadala Boutique Office, Borivali, Whitefield, Doddaballapur, and Vishrantwadi [14]. Second, Kanjurmarg's leasehold-to-freehold conversion missed June and December expectations [14]. Management warned that missing the December 31, 2026 window could trigger higher, unquantified government conversion charges [14]. Management also guided consolidated D/E back up toward 1.0x in FY27 to fund the launch wave [10][14].

book_paragraphs: If you want to know whether a real estate CEO is a disciplined operator or a perpetual optimist, ignore the five-year vision slides and build a simple walk-the-talk scorecard. Over the past four years, Ajmera's leadership has earned genuinely high marks on two fronts: balance-sheet repair and core-market sales execution. When management promised in FY23 to bring debt-to-equity well below 1.0x, they followed through—combining a ₹225 crore preferential equity raise with surging project collections to cut gearing from 1.13x all the way down to 0.44x by September 2026. When they guided for ₹1,600 crore of pre-sales in FY26, they beat it cleanly at ₹1,701 crore, powered by rapid absorption at Manhattan II and Solis Vikhroli.

Yet the same scorecard reveals a recurring blind spot: regulatory approval timelines. In FY25, management stood by a ₹1,350 crore pre-sales target even in Q3, only to finish around ₹1,084 crore because four planned launches slipped into the following year. Nowhere is this optimism bias clearer than at Kanjurmarg. Investors have been told since FY25 that the Kanjurmarg launch was 'a quarter or two away'—first Q1 FY26, then Q4 FY26, then H2 FY27—while the leasehold-to-freehold land conversion remained trapped in court and revenue-department processes as of November 2026. Management candidly admitted on the Q2 FY27 call that missing the December 31, 2026 conversion deadline could even raise the statutory conversion cost.

That brings you and I to the immediate operational test for FY27. In the first half of FY27 (April–September 2026), Ajmera clocked just ₹307 crore in pre-sales against a full-year target of ₹2,200 crore. That means nearly 86% of the annual goal is compressed into the second half, particularly Q4 FY27, when eight projects—led by the massive Wadala Boutique Office—are scheduled to hit the market. Even if one or two launches slip across the March 31 fiscal boundary, the underlying inventory is real; the question is whether investors will forgive another year of back-ended guidance and a planned rise in gearing back toward 1.0x.

At the same time, it is worth noticing what has quietly improved beneath the surface: average realizations doubled from ₹12,083 per square foot in FY21 to ₹25,770 per square foot in FY26, and collection efficiency climbed to 65%. That tells you Ajmera is not buying volume with distress discounts; it is selling higher-value central Mumbai inventory and collecting cash reliably from buyers.

book_callouts.title: Separating Timing Risk from Asset Value
book_callouts.text: A launch that slips from March to May does not destroy a land bank's economic value, but repeated timeline misses—paired with rising conversion fees at Kanjurmarg—explain why the market demands proof of execution before crediting full GDV.

book_callouts.title: The 86% H2 FY27 Hurdle
book_callouts.text: With ₹307 crore booked in H1 FY27, Ajmera needs ₹1,893 crore in H2 FY27 to hit its ₹2,200 crore guidance—leaving almost zero margin for municipal or RERA approval delays in Q4.

book_subsections.title: Why Collections Matter More Than Bookings
paragraphs: One encouraging detail in Ajmera's FY26–H1 FY27 numbers is the steady rise in cash collections. In FY26, collections surged 71% to ₹1,103 crore, and even in a quiet H1 FY27 for new launches (₹307 crore bookings), collections held at ₹363 crore because sold towers like Manhattan I and Sion/Vikhroli hit construction milestones.

That recurring collection engine is what funds construction without distressed borrowing, and it is the primary reason CRISIL reaffirmed its A-/Stable rating even as Ajmera prepares for an ambitious eight-project launch wave.
